title: Zoom Basic header and client_secret placeholders and public ids
summary: A scheme-only Basic header, placeholders, references, masked values, a client_secret field holding a placeholder or mask, a prose mention, and token requests that carry only the account id and client id.
rationale: The word Basic names a scheme and is also an everyday term, so prose or a header with no value is not a credential, and a placeholder, reference or masked display carries no value. The account id and the client id are public identifiers that sit beside the secret in the same requests.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: these inputs hold no credential value. That a placeholder, reference, masked or empty value, prose mention or public identifier is not a value is a project decision, not a Zoom statement.

sources.supports: The Basic Authorization header is your Client ID and Client Secret by a colon (:) and Base64 encoded. Use PKCE to enable user authorization with a public client ID an no client secret, without the need for a backend server.
sources.locator: Request an access token, App Type: General, Exchange authorization code for access token

sources.supports: Encode the client ID and client secret in base64 format (with a colon between them, e.g. client_id:client_secret). Set up your API request header and include your encoded client ID and client secret using the 'Basic' HTTP Authentication Scheme
sources.locator: Generate access token, To generate an access token, steps 1 and 2

sources.supports: When setting up OAuth for user authorization, the development client ID and client secret are used to generate access tokens. (example POST https://zoom.us/oauth/token, x-www-form-urlencoded, with grant_type, code, redirect_uri, client_id and client_secret fields)
sources.locator: Credentials in Development vs Production, When to use development credentials, Testing OAuth authentication
